title: SSE resume token leasing and backoff harmonization for partial-chunk idempotency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current SSE resume mechanism treats resume tokens as opaque identifiers with unlimited reuse; this leads to ambiguous replays when clients reconnect mid-chunk and causes either duplicate events or dropped partial output. We also have inconsistent client/server backoff behavior: clients use client-side exponential backoff while servers sometimes instruct different retry intervals, creating oscillation and capacity spikes.

Goal: Design and implement a server-driven 'resume token leasing' model that encodes an epoch and lease TTL, combined with a harmonized backoff negotiation (server-suggested backoff + client-jittered enforcement) to minimize duplicates, allow safe idempotent replays of partial chunks, and reduce reconnect storms across scaled hosts. Maintain compatibility with legacy resume tokens and allow feature-flagged rollout per customer/org.
acceptance_criteria: Server issues resume_token objects that include: token_id, sequence_watermark, lease_epoch, lease_ttl_iso8601 and optional server_nonce
Clients attempting resume must present token + lease_epoch; server validates lease_ttl and rejects expired leases with HTTP 409 (LeaseExpired) including suggested earliest_retry timestamp
Reconnect handshake supports server-suggested backoff via 'Retry-After' and 'X-RI-Backoff' headers; clients apply jittered enforcement and obey server-specified maximum retries per minute
Partial-chunk replay is idempotent: server replays from sequence_watermark and reuses stable chunk-boundary hints to avoid duplication of already-acknowledged frames
Legacy clients (resume_token_v1) can still resume but are mapped to conservative server-side semantics (short lease, stricter de-duplication) to avoid regressions
End-to-end tests covering normal resume, expired-lease, token-rotation, and multi-host failover exist in the integration suite
Metric coverage: resumed_connection_rate, lease_expiry_rate, duplicate_frame_rate, time_to_resume; alerts configured for duplicate_frame_rate > 0.1% and lease_expiry_rate growth > 2x baseline
tech_notes: Token format: base64url(JSON) signed with server key. Payload fields: {token_id, seq_watermark, epoch, ttl_seconds, server_nonce(optional)}. Signing prevents client tampering and allows stateless validation on scaled hosts.

Lease semantics: When a token is minted on initial connection, server records a short lease (default 30s) and includes ttl_seconds. On graceful disconnect client should include last-acked seq to request lease extension (POST /sse/extend). Unauthenticated resumption without valid lease -> HTTP 409.

Idempotency strategy: every chunk frame includes chunk_id + chunk_offset + cumulative_ack. On resume, server compares seq_watermark and chunk_offset to avoid re-emitting bytes already acked by the client. If watermark is in the middle of a chunk, server will re-send the chunk from chunk_offset; client must apply chunk-level dedupe by chunk_id and offset.

Backoff harmonization: server sends 'X-RI-Backoff: base=2s,max=120s,scale=linear' metadata during 5xx or capacity events. Clients compute backoff = min(max, base * 2^n) then apply +/- jitter(0..20%) but must not retry faster than server-specified base. Server-provided 'Retry-After' takes precedence for individual 503 responses.

Compatibility: Introduce resume_token_v2 while accepting v1. v1 tokens map to epoch 0 and default ttl 5s to force conservative replays. We will not revoke v1 tokens immediately but will mark them in telemetry to measure usage before eventual deprecation.

State storage: Prefer stateless token verification using signed tokens to avoid cross-host coordination. For lease extension and revocation we use a small, strongly-consistent store (etcd) for active_lease index keyed by token_id when extension frequency is high (to avoid long-lived leases overwhelming stateless model).
Security: Signed tokens prevent client forgery. Revoke path: admin revoke endpoint will mark token_id revoked in etcd; resumed attempts will return HTTP 401 (Revoked).

Failure modes and mitigation: If a client reconnects to a different host that has not seen the latest token (clock skew or delayed replication), the host will query the active_lease index; if unavailable, the host returns 202-Resume-Deferred with small backoff suggestion and correlation_id for debugging.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag controlled: resume_token_v2 on by default for internal orgs only
Canary: enable for 5 production orgs with high traffic, observe duplicate_frame_rate and lease_expiry_rate for 72h
Gradual ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 2 weeks if metrics stable
Fallback: server can opt-out per-org by downgrading token issuance to v1 semantics for 30 minutes
Post-mortem checklist: collect last-10 failed resumes per org and attach to incident dashboard
qa_tests: Integration test: resume mid-chunk -> server resumes from chunk_offset and client applies dedupe -> assert no duplicate data delivered
Load test: reconnect storm simulation across 1000 clients with harmonized backoff -> peak qps reduction compared to current baseline
Compatibility test: v1 client resumes against v2 server and receives conservative behavior (short ttl)
Chaos test: host failure during resume -> other host honors signed token and continues stream
monitoring_and_alerting: Create dashboards: Resumes by token_version, Resume Success Rate, Duplicate Frame Rate, Lease Expiry Rate
Alert: Duplicate Frame Rate > 0.1% sustained for 15m
Alert: Lease Expiry Rate jump > 2x baseline in any 1h window
